summary.text: Erik Underwood, an Approval Voting Party candidate and technology entrepreneur who says he spent eight years suing Bank of America in federal court, lost the November 3, 2026 election for governor of Colorado to Phil Weiser.
He ran on a joint ticket with Frank Atwood, on a child care program funded by a per-purchase charge, universal health care and ending the Taxpayer's Bill of Rights (TABOR).

paragraphs.text: Underwood says he grew up in housing projects, raised by a single mother, and that he worked in the U.S. Senate in Washington, D.C.
He also says he was a student junior prosecutor in the Atlanta City Solicitor's Office for five months.
His campaign biography describes eight years of federal court litigation against Bank of America Corporation across multiple circuits.
He is chairman of Illmatic Ventures and chief executive of My24HourNews.com and Vurbil.
Underwood sought the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate in Colorado in 2020 but was disqualified from the primary ballot.
In 2026 he was on the general-election ballot as the Approval Voting Party nominee for governor and did not appear on the June 30 Democratic primary ballot.

His campaign site lists a child care program funded by a 25-cent charge on each purchase, a plan for universal health care in Colorado, affordable home loans with a maximum of $2,500 down, and free college and trade school.
He received 0.4% of the vote to Phil Weiser's 61.1%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
